declarations.location: Section 5, Theorem 1, page 10; proof in Appendix B, pages 17-19
declarations.exact_game: BeeKemKiGame over the executable Figure 8 oracle environment, with bee_safe_kappa computed from the complete query log
declarations.query_bounds: actual bke_challenge_count <= c and bke_member_addition_count <= n with probability 1
declarations.reduction_loss: c * h, where beekem_is_ceil_log2 n h is executable and characterizes h = ceil(log2 n)
threat_model_boundary: adaptive reveal, challenge, and snapshot compromise
no arbitrary Byzantine deviation by an authorized member
declarations.normalization: Uniform centered bias abs(Pr[guess = bit] - 1/2) is used for KI-DCGKA, HKR-CKS, and MU-CPA. Page 10 prints raw success probability, while Appendix B pages 16-17 explicitly use absolute neighboring-game probability differences. Uniform doubling would cancel on both sides, so the theorem constants are unchanged.
declarations.machine_check_status: The games, safety predicate, counters, side-condition games, and interface are machine checked. Appendix B and its reduction witnesses BNike/BSe are imported, not machine checked.

non_claims: No concrete signature scheme is proved secure by this manifest; the exact primitive-game probabilities remain on the theorem right-hand side.
No concrete Rust serialization, hashing, persistence, erasure, crash-recovery, zeroization, or operating-system residue property is proved here.
Live-key and ungranted-content-key confidentiality are separate unfinished deliverables.
BeeKEM Appendix B and the internal construction of BNike and BSe are imported paper evidence, not machine-checked EasyCrypt reductions.

Page 10 prints a raw-success advantage definition inconsistent with Appendix B hybrid differences. The imported theorem uses the uniform centered interpretation and records this source-level normalization repair explicitly.
